column1: # Example Input Data for Crossover Detection
# Based on Lu et al. (2012) Science supplementary data format
# SNP genotype data from single sperm sequencing
#   chromosome     - Chromosome name (e.g., chr1, chr2, ..., chrX, chrY)
#   sperm_genotype - Sperm genotype at this position (A/C/G/T or N for missing)
#   diploid_genotype - Diploid (blood) genotype at this position
# Example data (first 20 SNPs for sperm S01 on chr1):
# Note: In real data, you would have ~100,000-500,000 SNPs per sperm genome
# The crossover points are where the sperm genotype switches from matching
# one parental haplotype to the other.
# Haplotype phasing information from parental/trio data
# Expected output format for crossover detection results
#   start_pos       - Start position of haplotype block
#   end_pos         - End position of haplotype block
# Expected output format for crossover statistics
#   total_crossovers    - Total number of crossovers detected
#   total_blocks        - Total number of haplotype blocks
#   mean_resolution_kb  - Mean crossover resolution in kilobases
#   mean_confidence     - Mean confidence score across all crossovers
#    - Lu et al. (2012) used MALBAC amplification followed by Illumina sequencing
#    - Total SNPs per sperm: ~100,000-500,000 heterozygous sites from diploid genome
#    - Filter SNPs with quality score < Q20
#    - Filter SNPs with coverage < 3x in diploid genome
#    - chrX/chrY: Only one copy in haploid sperm, analyze separately
#    - PAR (Pseudo-autosomal region): Recombines between X and Y
#    - Centromeric regions: Low SNP density, lower confidence
